BiblicalUsage: To gather grain, and the law uses it for the thief who gathers men. If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh merchandise of him, or selleth him, then that thief shall die. And the psalm of the harvest says the mower filleth not his hand with the grass of the housetops, nor he that bindeth sheaves his bosom; the word is the gathering, whether of sheaves or of stolen men.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for gathering grain carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two gatherings, that the sheaf-binder's arms are empty on the housetops and the man-stealer dies for treating a brother as a harvest.
